item.title: Obesity linked to up to 27% lower risk of death in dementia
item.description: A surprising study of more than 4,500 older adults found that people who were overweight or obese when diagnosed with dementia had a 16% to 27% lower risk of death than those at a normal weight. Researchers suspect that extra energy and muscle reserves may help patients survive the disease's toll on the body, although the reason for the survival advantage remains unclear. Fuente: ScienceDaily.

item.title: For nearly 2,000 years historians assumed Verica,was a man, archaeologist argues it was a woman
item.description: Archaeological studies now indicate that Verica, long regarded as a male figure, might have been a female monarch. This discovery challenges conventional beliefs about early British leaders, particularly regarding the likes of Boudica. Coin evidence featuring depictions that could signify a feminine identity adds weight to this theory. Such findings emphasize the importance of female authority in Iron Age Britain's political landscape. Fuente: The Times of India - World.
